statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.304 Part-II; Dowry Prohibition Act s.3, s.6
aggravating_circumstances: Motive of transferring property, conduct of appellant, absence of explanation for burn injuries
high_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 304 Part-II of the IPC
offence_finally_established: Murder under Section 304 Part-II of the IPC
neutral_facts: The accused, the husband of the deceased, was charged with causing her death by setting her on fire with kerosene. The deceased provided a dying declaration to a police official, which was endorsed by the attending doctor. The accused was charged under Sections 302 and 304 Part-II of the IPC, as well as Sections 3 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act. The prosecution's case was supported by the deceased's dying declaration and the attending doctor's endorsement. The trial court acquitted the accused, citing the absence of the doctor's endorsement and the deceased's alleged sedation. The High Court overturned the acquittal, finding the evidence of the deceased's fitness to make a dying declaration and the absence of an explanation for the burn injuries as sufficient to establish guilt. The accused was found to have absconded and failed to provide an alibi, which contributed to the High Court's conviction.
